item.title: Conserving a Revolution
item.description: Argues that American conservatism’s real tension is not the mere fact of conserving a revolutionary regime, but the need to rank several conflicting inheritances: colonial constitutional tradition, universal natural rights, republican institutions, unequal historical practices, and later American social traditions.

item.title: The Yankee Leviathan: Grandeur and Self-Indictment in Moby-Dick
item.description: Reads Moby-Dick as a double-action text that magnifies New England and American moral, intellectual, commercial, and political authority while building its own countercase through cosmopolitan labor, democratic federation, epistemic incompletion, anti-imperial property satire, and the destruction of Ahab’s command regime.
